minigame.MG-01.name: Unit Converter Sprint
minigame.MG-01.how_to_play: Swipe each value to its matching SI value before it reaches the "upload" line.
minigame.MG-01.detail: Engineering values fly in with mixed units (lbf, N, ft, m, psi, kPa). Swipe each to the matching SI value before it reaches the "upload" line.
minigame.MG-01.boost: Reliability (removes a hidden "unit error" software fault) → Bronze: uncertainty −20%; Silver: −40%; Gold: Reliability Shield.
minigame.MG-01.reward.1: Removes a hidden "unit error" software fault
minigame.MG-01.relaxed: Values move toward the upload line more slowly.
minigame.MG-01.one_button: Values stop one at a time and the possible SI values are highlighted in turn; press the button on the match. No swiping.
minigame.MG-02.name: Rocket Equation Balance
minigame.MG-02.how_to_play: Drop propellant blocks on the scale to bring the Δv needle into the target band with the fewest blocks.
minigame.MG-02.detail: A balance scale: drop propellant blocks on one side and watch the Δv needle. Each block adds less Δv than the one before (logarithm!). Hit the target Δv band with the fewest blocks.
minigame.MG-02.relaxed: The target Δv band is wider and the timer is longer.
minigame.MG-02.one_button: Press the button to drop one block; stop pressing when the needle is in the band.
minigame.MG-03.name: Weld Inspector
minigame.MG-03.when: Build, during structural material integration or static fire test.
minigame.MG-03.how_to_play: Sweep a finger over the X-ray images of tank welds and tap the hidden porosity and cracks, avoiding false alarms.
minigame.MG-03.detail: Scan X-ray images of tank welds by sweeping a finger; tap the hidden porosity and cracks. Avoid false alarms.
minigame.MG-03.success: Find ≥ 80% of defects with ≤ 1 false alarm.
minigame.MG-03.fact: Large rocket tanks are joined with friction stir welding, which stirs metal together without melting it.
minigame.MG-03.relaxed: Defects are larger and the scan time is longer.
minigame.MG-03.one_button: The scanner sweeps along the weld by itself; press the button when it passes over a defect.
minigame.MG-04.name: Orientation Check
minigame.MG-04.how_to_play: Spin each sensor and connector to match the drawing, and press "drawing error" when the drawing itself is wrong.
minigame.MG-04.detail: Sensors and connectors appear rotated; spin each to match the drawing. Some drawings are wrong: spot them with a "drawing error" button.
minigame.MG-04.success: All correct, including catching the drawing error.
minigame.MG-04.boost: Parachute & sensor reliability; Gold gives a Reliability Shield for the descent phase.
minigame.MG-04.relaxed: The timer is longer and a part snaps into place when it is close to the drawing.
minigame.MG-04.one_button: Each part turns step by step and then shows a "drawing error" choice; press the button on the right one.
minigame.MG-05.name: Clean Room
minigame.MG-05.when: Build, science payload integration (or Contamination anomaly).
minigame.MG-05.how_to_play: Wipe the drifting particles off the camera lens and mirror with gentle strokes; wiping too hard scratches.
minigame.MG-05.detail: Particles drift onto a camera lens and mirror; wipe them with gentle strokes. Wiping too hard scratches.
minigame.MG-05.fact: Spacecraft are built in clean rooms, where air is filtered and workers wear "bunny suits", because one fingerprint can ruin an optic.
minigame.MG-05.relaxed: Particles drift more slowly and the wiping pressure is more forgiving.
minigame.MG-05.one_button: A swab moves across the optic by itself; hold the button to wipe gently and release over clean glass.
minigame.MG-06.name: Shake Table
minigame.MG-06.how_to_play: Move your damper slider to keep the resonance meter out of the red as the frequencies sweep.
minigame.MG-06.detail: A payload shakes at rising frequencies. Each player controls one damper slider; keep the resonance meter out of the red as frequencies sweep.
minigame.MG-06.success: Per player: their damper stays in the green ≥ 80% of the time.
minigame.MG-06.fact: Spacecraft are shaken on vibration tables to make sure they survive the violent ride to orbit.
minigame.MG-06.relaxed: The frequency sweep is slower and the green zone is wider.
minigame.MG-06.one_button: The damper slides back and forth by itself; press the button to stop it in the green.
minigame.MG-07.name: Go/No-Go Poll
minigame.MG-07.how_to_play: When FLIGHT calls your console, check your 3 readings against the launch-commit limits and answer GO or NO-GO within 5 s.
minigame.MG-07.detail: FLIGHT calls each console in turn. Each player sees 3 readings for their console (e.g. winds aloft, LOX temperature, battery voltage) with the launch-commit limits. Answer GO or NO-GO correctly within 5 s.
minigame.MG-07.boost: Removes countdown holds; Gold: launch at the optimal second of the window (+Δv saved).
minigame.MG-07.reward.2: Launch at the optimal second of the window (+Δv saved)
minigame.MG-07.relaxed: Each player has more time to answer.
minigame.MG-07.one_button: GO and NO-GO are highlighted in turn; press the button on your answer.
minigame.MG-08b.name: Propellant Loading
minigame.MG-08b.how_to_play: Tap the valves to keep the tank fill rate in the target band while boil-off vents.
minigame.MG-08b.detail: Keep a tank fill rate in the target band by tapping valves while boil-off vents. Overfill vents propellant; underfill causes a hold.
minigame.MG-08b.fact: Super-cold propellants boil continuously, so tanks are "topped off" until just before launch.
minigame.MG-08b.relaxed: The target band is wider and boil-off is slower.
minigame.MG-08b.one_button: Hold the button to open the fill valve and release to close it (or switch to toggle).
minigame.MG-08.name: Max Q Throttle Bucket
minigame.MG-08.how_to_play: Slide your throttle so the vehicle's stress line stays inside the safe band as dynamic pressure rises.
minigame.MG-08.detail: A dynamic-pressure curve rises. Slide your throttle so the vehicle's stress line stays inside a safe band. Too low wastes time against gravity; too high overloads.
minigame.MG-08.relaxed: The safe band is wider and the curve rises more slowly.
minigame.MG-08.one_button: Hold the button to throttle down and release to throttle up (or switch to toggle).
minigame.MG-09.name: Gravity Turn Tracer
minigame.MG-09.how_to_play: Trace the ideal ascent curve with a finger as the trajectory scrolls.
minigame.MG-09.detail: Trace the ideal ascent curve with a finger as the trajectory scrolls. The team's average error steers the real rocket.
minigame.MG-09.fact: Rockets don't fly straight up for long. A gravity turn lets gravity bend the path toward horizontal and saves fuel.
minigame.MG-09.relaxed: The curve scrolls more slowly and a larger deviation is allowed.
minigame.MG-09.one_button: The marker follows the curve by itself; press the button at each pitch cue to keep it on the line.
minigame.MG-10a.name: Staging Timing
minigame.MG-10a.how_to_play: Tap SEPARATE in the green window just after engine cutoff, then IGNITE after the propellant settles.
minigame.MG-10a.detail: The engine-cutoff light flashes and propellant gauges drain. Everyone taps SEPARATE in the green window just after cutoff, then IGNITE after settling. The tighter the team's timing, the better.
minigame.MG-10a.success: Each player taps inside the window (±0.3 s).
minigame.MG-10a.boost: Δv Bonus; Gold also prevents recontact entirely.
minigame.MG-10a.one_button: One button does both steps: press once to SEPARATE and once more to IGNITE.
minigame.MG-10.name: Fairing Catch
minigame.MG-10.how_to_play: Steer your recovery boat to keep the net under your fairing half as it drifts down.
minigame.MG-10.detail: Two fairing halves drift down under parafoils. Players steer recovery boats (in teams) to keep each half over the net.
minigame.MG-10.success: Your boat stays under its target ≥ 70%.
minigame.MG-10.fact: Fairings are expensive enough that some companies recover and reuse them.
minigame.MG-10.relaxed: The fairing halves drift more slowly and the net is larger.
minigame.MG-10.one_button: The boat steers toward its target while the button is held and drifts when it is released.
minigame.MG-11.name: Pogo Damper
minigame.MG-11.when: F5 (if pogo triggered, chance raised without a pogo test).
minigame.MG-11.how_to_play: Tap in counter-rhythm to the lengthwise bouncing of the vehicle to cancel it.
minigame.MG-11.detail: The vehicle bounces lengthwise. Tap in counter-rhythm to the oscillation to cancel it. The more players in sync, the faster it dampens.
minigame.MG-11.success: Each player's taps are opposite in phase to the oscillation for ≥ 70% of beats.
minigame.MG-11.relaxed: The oscillation is slower and the timing window around each beat is wider.
minigame.MG-11.one_button: Already one button: tap on the counter-beat. A visual metronome marks each beat.
minigame.MG-12.name: Engine-Out Rebalance
minigame.MG-12.when: F5/F7 if an engine fails in a cluster.
minigame.MG-12.how_to_play: Adjust the throttle and gimbal of your engine to balance the thrust around the center of mass and keep the rocket straight.
minigame.MG-12.detail: Each player controls one remaining engine's throttle/gimbal; balance the thrust around the center of mass to keep the rocket straight.
minigame.MG-12.success: Your engine keeps the net torque near zero.
minigame.MG-12.boost: Recovers lost Δv; Gold restores the planned trajectory.
minigame.MG-12.relaxed: Thrust changes more slowly and the zone that counts as zero torque is wider.
minigame.MG-12.one_button: The throttle of your engine sweeps up and down by itself; press the button to lock it when the torque needle is centered.
minigame.MG-13.name: Ground Station Pass
minigame.MG-13.how_to_play: Keep your antenna reticle on the ground station as it arcs across the horizon.
minigame.MG-13.detail: A ground station sweeps across the horizon. Keep your antenna reticle on it as it arcs. Packets fill your data bar while locked.
minigame.MG-13.relaxed: The station moves more slowly and the lock circle is larger.
minigame.MG-13.one_button: The antenna tracks by itself but drifts off; press the button to re-center it on the station.
minigame.MG-14.name: Debris Dodge
minigame.MG-14.how_to_play: Choose the smallest burn direction and duration that clears the collision probability threshold.
minigame.MG-14.detail: Debris tracks approach on a radar. Choose the smallest burn direction and duration that clears the collision probability threshold. Overburning wastes fuel.
minigame.MG-14.success: Safe miss with ≤ 1.2× the minimum Δv.
minigame.MG-14.relaxed: There is more time to choose and the burn options are shown as a short list.
minigame.MG-14.one_button: Burn options are highlighted in turn; press the button on the smallest one that clears the threshold.
minigame.MG-15.name: Solar Wing Deploy
minigame.MG-15.when: F8 (satellite or capsule with deployable arrays).
minigame.MG-15.how_to_play: Release your hinge in the order shown on the diagram, then rotate the wing to face the Sun.
minigame.MG-15.detail: Each player releases one hinge in the correct order shown by a diagram; then everyone rotates the wing to face the Sun as the spacecraft turns.
minigame.MG-15.success: Your hinge released in order + Sun-pointing ≥ 80%.
minigame.MG-15.relaxed: Each hinge waits longer for its release and the Sun-pointing zone is wider.
minigame.MG-15.one_button: Press the button when your hinge is highlighted; the wing then turns by itself and each press nudges it back toward the Sun.
minigame.MG-16.name: Station Docking
minigame.MG-16.how_to_play: Line up the crosshairs with the translation thrusters while keeping your closing speed under the limit.
minigame.MG-16.detail: Line up crosshairs using translation thrusters while closing speed must stay under a limit (displayed in cm/s). Inertia is real: things keep moving until you thrust the other way.
minigame.MG-16.success: Contact with alignment error < 10 cm and speed < 10 cm/s.
minigame.MG-16.boost: Precision + Score Multiplier; Gold enables the stretch objective.
minigame.MG-16.relaxed: The alignment target is larger and the spacecraft drifts more slowly.
minigame.MG-16.one_button: The thrusters correct the alignment by themselves; press the button to fire a braking pulse and keep the closing speed under the limit.
minigame.MG-17.name: Alarm Triage
minigame.MG-17.when: F8 or descent (guaranteed if "Software Bug Found" was accepted).
minigame.MG-17.how_to_play: Drag each alarm code to IGNORE, MONITOR or ACT according to the role cheat sheet.
minigame.MG-17.detail: Alarm codes flood in. Drag each to IGNORE, MONITOR or ACT according to the role cheat sheet. Program alarms that mean "computer is busy, still working" can be safely continued.
minigame.MG-17.one_button: IGNORE, MONITOR and ACT are highlighted in turn for each alarm; press the button on your choice.
minigame.MG-18.name: Eclipse Power Juggle
minigame.MG-18.how_to_play: Switch the spacecraft loads on and off to keep the battery above the red line through the eclipse while critical heaters stay on.
minigame.MG-18.detail: Toggle spacecraft loads (heaters, radio, instrument) on/off to keep the battery above the red line through the eclipse while keeping critical heaters on.
minigame.MG-18.success: Battery stays above minimum, critical loads always on.
minigame.MG-18.boost: Power margin; Data Multiplier (instrument stayed on longer).
minigame.MG-18.one_button: The loads are highlighted in turn; press the button to switch the highlighted load on or off.
minigame.MG-19.name: Scrubber Fix
minigame.MG-19.how_to_play: Drag your spare part into the right slot to help build an adapter that connects a square filter to a round socket.
minigame.MG-19.detail: CO₂ rising. Players receive random "spare parts" (hose, tape, card, bag, sock) and must collectively assemble an adapter connecting a square filter to a round socket by dragging parts into slots.
minigame.MG-19.success: The adapter is completed; each player who placed a correct part succeeds.
minigame.MG-19.relaxed: CO₂ rises more slowly, so there is more time to place the parts.
minigame.MG-19.one_button: The slots are highlighted in turn; press the button to put your part in the highlighted slot.
minigame.MG-20.name: Deorbit Burn
minigame.MG-20.how_to_play: Hold the burn button while the periapsis marker drops and release when it is inside the target band.
minigame.MG-20.detail: Hold the burn button while the periapsis marker drops; release when it's inside the target band. Team median result sets the real burn.
minigame.MG-20.fact: To come home, a spacecraft fires its engines backward to slow down, which lowers its orbit into the atmosphere.
minigame.MG-20.relaxed: The target band is wider and the marker drops more slowly.
minigame.MG-20.one_button: Already one button. Hold-to-burn can switch to press to start and press to stop.
minigame.MG-21.name: Science Capture
minigame.MG-21.when: F8 (C1 and other observation contracts), several times.
minigame.MG-21.how_to_play: Frame and snap the targets as they pass under the ground track, avoiding clouds unless you chose radar.
minigame.MG-21.detail: The ground track scrolls over Earth. Frame and snap targets (hurricane, wildfire, glacier, city lights, algae bloom) as they pass, avoiding clouds unless you chose radar.
minigame.MG-21.relaxed: The ground track scrolls more slowly and the frame is larger.
minigame.MG-21.one_button: The camera frames each target by itself; press the button to snap while the target is in frame.
minigame.MG-22.name: Entry Corridor
minigame.MG-22.how_to_play: Keep the angle icon of the capsule inside the narrow corridor: not too steep and not too shallow.
minigame.MG-22.detail: Keep the capsule's angle icon inside a narrow corridor. Too steep and the heat bar fills; too shallow and the capsule skips back to space.
minigame.MG-22.one_button: Hold the button to steepen the angle and release to let it shallow (or switch to toggle).
minigame.MG-23.name: Parachute Sequence
minigame.MG-23.how_to_play: Deploy your parachute exactly when its altitude/speed gate lights.
minigame.MG-23.detail: Each player owns one parachute stage (cover chutes, drogues, pilots, mains; extra players get backups). Deploy yours exactly when the altitude/speed gate lights; deploying early tears the chute, late gives a hard landing.
minigame.MG-23.success: Your chute opens in its gate.
minigame.MG-23.boost: Softer landing (Crew Morale, recovery refund) + Score Multiplier.
minigame.MG-23.one_button: Already one button: press when your gate lights.
minigame.MG-24.name: Hoverslam
minigame.MG-24.how_to_play: Tap IGNITE at the right altitude so the velocity of the booster reaches zero exactly at the ground.
minigame.MG-24.detail: The booster plummets. Tap IGNITE at the right altitude so velocity reaches zero exactly at the ground. A ghost shows the ideal.
minigame.MG-24.fact: Boosters can't throttle down enough to hover, so they light at the last moment and reach zero velocity right at touchdown, a "hoverslam".
minigame.MG-24.relaxed: The ghost stays visible and the ignition window is wider.
minigame.MG-24.one_button: Already one button: press IGNITE once.
minigame.MG-25.name: Reacquire Signal
minigame.MG-25.how_to_play: Turn the tuning dial to find the beacon frequency of the capsule, then press LOCK.
minigame.MG-25.detail: Phones show static. Turn a tuning dial to find the capsule's beacon frequency by ear/visual waveform, then press LOCK.
minigame.MG-25.boost: Precision (recovery forces dispatched early) + Crew Morale.
minigame.MG-25.relaxed: The beacon is stronger and the lock zone on the dial is wider.
minigame.MG-25.one_button: The dial sweeps by itself; press LOCK when the waveform peaks.
minigame.MG-26.name: Seven Minutes of Terror
minigame.MG-26.when: C7 Mars entry, descent and landing.
minigame.MG-26.how_to_play: Before entry, place your step of the landing sequence in the right order with the right timing, then watch the result arrive.
minigame.MG-26.detail: Because of the light-time delay, you can't fly it live. Before entry, the team arranges the EDL sequence cards (heat shield → parachute → separate shield → radar → descent engines → sky crane → cut cables) with timing. Each player programs their step, then everyone watches the result arrive.
minigame.MG-26.success: Your step is correct in order and timing.
minigame.MG-26.relaxed: There is more time to program and the timing window of each step is wider.
minigame.MG-26.one_button: The places in the sequence are highlighted in turn; press the button to put your step there.
minigame.MG-27.name: Recovery Team
minigame.MG-27.how_to_play: Follow the beacon signal to the capsule and arrive in order: swimmers, flotation collar, ship.
minigame.MG-27.detail: Players crew helicopters and boats; find the capsule using a beacon signal and arrive in order: swimmers, flotation collar, ship.
minigame.MG-27.success: Your unit arrives in the correct order.
minigame.MG-27.fact: Recovery teams practice for months so they can reach and secure a capsule within minutes of splashdown.
minigame.MG-27.relaxed: The beacon is easier to follow and there is more time to arrive.
minigame.MG-27.one_button: Your unit steers toward the beacon by itself; press the button to set off when it is your turn.
minigame.MG-28.name: Root Cause Investigation
minigame.MG-28.when: After a failure or major anomaly (debrief).
minigame.MG-28.how_to_play: Combine your telemetry cards with those of your teammates to build the chain of evidence that leads to the root cause.
minigame.MG-28.detail: Telemetry cards (pressure spike, temperature drop, vibration, software log) are dealt to players. Together, they assemble the chain of evidence that leads to the root cause.
minigame.MG-28.fact: Every real failure is followed by an investigation board that finds the root cause so it never happens again.
minigame.MG-28.boost: Lessons Learned card quality (Gold = permanent free fix + Codex badge).
minigame.MG-28.relaxed: There is more time to discuss and one clue card is marked as the starting point.
minigame.MG-28.one_button: The places in the chain of evidence are highlighted in turn; press the button to put your card there.
minigame.MG-29.name: Predict the Physics (bonus round)
minigame.MG-29.how_to_play: Choose your prediction before the animation plays.
minigame.MG-29.detail: Quick visual predictions: "Which falls faster in a vacuum: a hammer or a feather?" Choose before the animation plays.
minigame.MG-29.relaxed: There is more time to choose before the animation plays.
minigame.MG-29.one_button: The answers are highlighted in turn; press the button on your prediction.
minigame.MG-30.name: Mission Patch Design (cosmetic)
minigame.MG-30.how_to_play: Contribute one patch element (shape, symbol, color or motto), then vote on the final patch.
minigame.MG-30.detail: Each player contributes one patch element (shape, symbol, color, motto from a list). The team votes on the final patch.
minigame.MG-30.boost: Cosmetic only; the patch appears on the rocket and debrief.
minigame.MG-30.reward.1: Cosmetic only; the patch appears on the rocket and debrief
minigame.MG-30.relaxed: Nothing is timed against the player; the timer is longer.
minigame.MG-30.one_button: The patch elements are highlighted in turn; press the button to pick one.
fact.F01.text: NASA's Mars Climate Orbiter was lost in 1999 because one team used pound-force seconds while another expected newton-seconds.
fact.F01.source: NASA, Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board Phase I Report, 1999
fact.F02.text: The Tsiolkovsky rocket equation: more fuel means more mass to push, so returns shrink. That's why rockets have stages.
fact.F02.detail: The Tsiolkovsky rocket equation: Δv = Isp · g0 · ln(m0/mf). More fuel means more mass to push, so returns shrink. That's why rockets have stages.
fact.F02.source: NASA Science, Basics of Space Flight, Chapter 3: Gravity & Mechanics; NASA Glenn, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics: Ideal Rocket Equation and Stages
fact.F03.text: Staging drops empty tanks and engines so the rest of the rocket doesn't haul dead weight. Propellant must settle before the next engine lights.
fact.F03.source: NASA Glenn, Beginner's Guide to Rockets: Balloon Staging; NASA, Saturn I SA-8 Functional Systems Description Vol. X (SDES-64-414), 1964
fact.F04.text: Many rockets throttle down near Max Q, the moment of peak aerodynamic stress, often about a minute after liftoff.
fact.F04.source: NASA/USA, Space Shuttle Day-of-Launch Trajectory Design Operations, 2011; NASA, CHANGO: Boost Stage Guidance of the Space Launch System; NASA, SpaceX CRS-6 Press Kit, 2015
fact.F05.text: Orbital speed in low Earth orbit is about 7 to 8 km/s.
fact.F05.source: NASA Orbital Debris Program Office, Frequently Asked Questions
fact.F06.text: Gravity at the altitude of the ISS is about 90% of surface gravity; astronauts float because they're falling around Earth.
fact.F06.detail: Myth: there's no gravity on the ISS. Fact: it's ~90% of surface gravity; astronauts float because they're falling around Earth.
fact.F07.text: Pogo is a feedback loop between structural vibration, propellant flow and thrust. Apollo 13's second stage shut down its center engine because of severe pogo.
fact.F07.source: NASA, C. Larsen, NASA Experience with Pogo in Human Spaceflight Vehicles (NTRS 20080018689), 2008; NASA, Report of Apollo 13 Review Board, 1970
fact.F08.text: In 2012, a Falcon 9 lost an engine during ascent and still delivered its primary payload, thanks to engine-out capability.
fact.F08.source: NASA Office of Inspector General, Commercial Cargo: NASA's Management of COTS and ISS Commercial Resupply Contracts (IG-13-016), 2013
fact.F09.text: NASA's Deep Space Network uses three sites (California, Spain, Australia) about 120° apart, so a spacecraft is always in view of one.
fact.F09.detail: Satellites can only talk to a ground station when it's in view. NASA's Deep Space Network uses three sites (California, Spain, Australia) about 120° apart so a spacecraft is always in view of one.
fact.F09.source: NASA Space Communications and Navigation, What is the Deep Space Network? and Where is the DSN Located?
fact.F10.text: The ISS has made 41 debris-avoidance maneuvers since 1999. By 2026, more than 34,000 objects in Earth orbit had been cataloged.
fact.F10.source: NASA Orbital Debris Program Office, Frequently Asked Questions (2026)
fact.F11.text: Sunlight near Earth delivers about 1,361 W per square meter; modern space solar cells convert roughly 30% of it.
fact.F11.source: NASA Goddard, Solar Irradiance Science; NASA Small Spacecraft Systems Virtual Institute, State-of-the-Art: 3.0 Power
fact.F12.text: Spacecraft dock at a crawl, a few centimeters per second, because in space nothing stops on its own (Newton's first law).
fact.F12.source: NASA, STS-96 Press Kit: First Visit to an Outpost in Orbit, 1999
fact.F13.text: During the Apollo 11 landing, "1202" alarms warned the computer was overloaded, but its software kept the most important tasks running and the landing continued.
fact.F13.detail: During the Apollo 11 landing, "1202" alarms warned that the computer was overloaded, but its software kept the most important tasks running and the landing continued.
fact.F13.source: NASA, Apollo 11 Lunar Surface Journal: Program Alarms; NASA History, 50 Years Ago: One Small Step, One Giant Leap, 2019
fact.F14.text: In low Earth orbit a spacecraft can spend about 35 minutes of each ~90-minute orbit in Earth's shadow, running on batteries.
fact.F14.source: NASA Glenn, Raffaelle et al., Mission Applicability Assessment of Integrated Power Components and Systems (NASA/CP-2002-211831), 2002; NASA Science, Hubble Electrical Power
fact.F15.text: On Apollo 13, ground engineers invented a way to fit square CO₂ filters into round sockets using items aboard, and the crew built it.
fact.F15.detail: On Apollo 13, engineers on the ground invented a way to fit square CO₂ filters into round sockets using items aboard, and the crew built it.
fact.F15.source: NASA History, "Houston, We've Had a Problem"
fact.F16.text: Landsat satellites have imaged Earth's land surface continuously since 1972, tracking change over decades.
fact.F17.text: Returning capsules must hit a narrow "entry corridor": Apollo 13 had to enter between 5.25° and 7.4° below horizontal.
fact.F17.source: NASA JSC, Apollo 13 Guidance, Navigation, and Control Challenges (AIAA 2009-6455), 2009
fact.F18.text: Orion uses 11 parachutes in a precise sequence to slow from hundreds of km/h to about 30 km/h for splashdown.
fact.F18.source: NASA, Orion Parachute Tests Prove Out Complex System for Human Deep Space Missions
fact.F19.text: During reentry, superheated plasma surrounds the capsule and blocks radio. Apollo crews had several minutes of silence.
fact.F19.source: NASA JPL, Morabito, The Spacecraft Communications Blackout Problem Encountered during Passage or Entry of Planetary Atmospheres (IPN Progress Report 42-150), 2002
fact.F20.text: Radio signals take several minutes (about 3 to 22, depending on planet positions) to travel between Earth and Mars, so landers must land themselves.
fact.F20.source: NASA Science, Speaking Percy's Language: How to Talk so Perseverance Will Listen
fact.F21.text: The Genesis sample-return capsule crashed in 2004 because a design error put its gravity-switch sensors in the wrong orientation, so its parachutes never deployed.
fact.F21.source: NASA Science, Genesis mission page; NASA, Genesis Mishap Investigation Board Report, 2006
fact.F22.text: Ariane 5 Flight 501 (1996) suffered a software overflow: a number too big for its variable.
fact.F22.source: ESA/CNES, Ariane 5 Flight 501 Failure: Report by the Inquiry Board, 1996
fact.F23.text: Two NASA climate satellites (OCO in 2009, Glory in 2011) were lost when their fairings didn't separate.
fact.F23.source: NASA, NASA Investigative Summary: Taurus XL T8 and T9 Mission Failures, 2019
fact.F24.text: The International Space Station orbits at 51.6° inclination partly so that launches from Baikonur could reach it.
fact.F24.source: NASA, Stockman, International Space Station Systems Engineering Case Study (Air Force Center for Systems Engineering); NASA Earth Observatory, Catalog of Earth Satellite Orbits
fact.F25.text: Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact, no igniter needed: a good choice for Apollo's engine that had to work to bring astronauts home from the Moon.
fact.F25.detail: Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact, with no igniter needed. That made them a good choice for Apollo's engine that had to work to bring astronauts home from the Moon.
fact.F25.source: NASA History, 60 Years Ago: First Test Firing of the Apollo Service Propulsion System, 2024
fact.F26.text: F-1 engineers set off small bombs inside test engines to make sure combustion instabilities damped out.
fact.F26.source: NASA History, Solving Combustion Instability and Saving America's First Trips to the Moon
fact.F27.text: The Soviet N1 rocket had 30 first-stage engines; all four launches ended in first-stage failures, several tied to its engines and engine control system.
fact.F27.source: NASA History, Mir Hardware Heritage, Part 1: Soyuz
fact.F28.text: Stardust made the fastest reentry, at about 12.9 km/s.
fact.F28.source: NASA/JPL, Stardust Sample Return Press Kit, January 2006; NASA Langley, Reconstruction of the Stardust Entry, 2007
fact.F29.text: NASA's LOFTID tested an inflatable heat shield in 2022.
fact.F29.source: NASA Ames, LOFTID Inflatable Heat Shield Test A Success, Early Results Show, 2022
fact.F30.text: In 2018, a Soyuz booster failed about two minutes after launch; the ascent was aborted, the spacecraft separated, and both crew landed safely.
fact.F30.source: NASA Space Station blog, Statement on Soyuz MS-10 Launch Abort, Launch Update and Station Crew Busy With Science After Aborted Launch Ascent, October 2018
fact.F31.text: Apollo 12 was struck by lightning twice during launch in 1969, which is why lightning rules matter.
fact.F31.detail: Real launches use launch-commit criteria for weather, winds and hardware. Apollo 12 was struck by lightning twice during launch in 1969, which is why lightning rules matter.
fact.F31.source: NASA, A History of the Lightning Launch Commit Criteria and the Lightning Advisory Panel for America's Space Program (NASA/SP-2010-216283), 2010
fact.F32.text: On Apollo 15, David Scott dropped a hammer and a feather on the Moon, and they hit the ground together.
fact.F32.source: NASA NSSDCA, The Apollo 15 Hammer-Feather Drop
fact.F33.text: Curiosity's radioisotope generator (an MMRTG) produced about 110 W at launch.
fact.F33.source: NASA/JPL, Mars Science Laboratory/Curiosity Fact Sheet
fact.F34.text: The first of NASA's TDRS relay satellites was launched in 1983.
fact.F34.source: NASA Space Communications and Navigation, History of the Networks
fact.F35.text: NASA's laser (optical) communications include LCRD (2021) and DSOC on Psyche (2023).
fact.F35.source: NASA, Laser Communications Relay Demonstration (LCRD) Overview; NASA/JPL, Psyche Launch Press Kit: Deep Space Optical Communications
fact.F36.text: NASA crews have designed their own mission patches since the Gemini program.
fact.F36.source: NASA, Gemini V: Paving the Way for Long Duration Spaceflight; NASA History, Symbols of NASA
fact.F37.text: In 1985, a faulty sensor shut down one of STS-51F's main engines; the Shuttle performed an abort to orbit and the mission still succeeded.
fact.F37.source: NASA, STS-51F mission page; NASA JSC, Henderson and Nguyen, Space Shuttle Abort Evolution (AIAA SPACE 2011)
fact.F38.text: Perseverance used terrain-relative navigation to avoid hazards in 2021.
fact.F38.source: NASA STMD, Impact Story: Terrain Relative Navigation; NASA/JPL, Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, 2021
fact.F39.text: The Saturn V stood 111 m (363 feet) tall, about the height of a 36-story building.
fact.F39.source: NASA, What Was the Saturn V? (Grades 5-8)
fact.F40.text: Launch windows to Mars open about every 26 months.
fact.F40.source: NASA JPL, The Launch Is Approaching for NASA's Next Mars Rover, Perseverance, 2020
